prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: Cc1cc(C#N)cc(C)c1Oc1nc(Nc2ccc(C#N)cc2)nc(N)c1Br
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL247

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of HIV1 wild-type reverse transcriptase using [3H]dTTP by scintillation counting
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of recombinant wild type p66/p51 HIV1 reverse transcriptase incubated for 40 mins by picogreen dye-based spectrofluorometric analysis
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Human immunodeficiency virus 1

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.6, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 of the same compound against wild-type HIV-1 reverse transcriptase with high confidence scores, and while the detection methods differ (scintillation counting vs. picogreen spectrofluorometry), they both quantify polymerase activity inhibition, so results are expected to be broadly comparable within 0.3 log units."}

parsed.reason: Both assays measure IC50 of the same compound against wild-type HIV-1 reverse transcriptase with high confidence scores, and while the detection methods differ (scintillation counting vs. picogreen spectrofluorometry), they both quantify polymerase activity inhibition, so results are expected to be broadly comparable within 0.3 log units.
